claim: ElastiCache Serverless continuously tracks CPU, memory and network use. When one is constrained, it scales out by adding a new shard and redistributing data to it, without any downtime to your application.

claim: With data tiering, when memory (DRAM) is fully consumed ElastiCache uses an LRU algorithm to move infrequently accessed items from memory to SSD. When data on SSD is accessed, ElastiCache automatically and asynchronously moves it back to memory before processing the request.
question: How does ElastiCache data tiering decide what moves from memory to SSD?

values.display: move infrequently accessed items from memory to SSD
automatically and asynchronously moves it back to memory

qualifiers.scope: Valkey and Redis OSS clusters with data tiering
qualifiers.condition: when available memory is fully consumed

evidence.quote: On ElastiCache clusters with data tiering, ElastiCache monitors the last access time of every item it stores. When available memory (DRAM) is fully consumed, ElastiCache uses a least-recently used (LRU) algorithm to automatically move infrequently accessed items from memory to SSD. When data on SSD is subsequently accessed, ElastiCache automatically and asynchronously moves it back to memory before processing the request.
